CHAMBER_STYLE: a neon-lit rave arena with shifting walls
a flooded cistern with knee-deep black water
a bone-white amphitheater ringed with viewing screens
a rusted industrial press room, machinery still running
a mock courtroom, jury box full of the boss's kin
a circular pit with a retractable floor
an abandoned goblin foundry, forges banked but warm
a mushroom-choked grotto lit by bioluminescent rot
a converted safe room, the door now permanently open
NOTABLE_FEATURES: A collapsed safe room, door blown outward. Something got in.
A functioning mob market. Prices are in teeth.
A shrine to a god the dungeon declines to name.
An abandoned goblin workshop with a half-built vehicle.
A viewing-screen wall that replays crawler deaths from this neighborhood.
A long, straight tunnel with no cover. Obvious kill zone.
A drowned section requiring a swim or a long detour.
A crawler camp, recently abandoned. Supplies scattered. Blood.
A locked door that only opens for a party of four or more.
A chasm bridged by a single rope. The mobs cut it if they see you.
A nest. Do not disturb the nest.
A dead boss chamber from a previous neighborhood boss, already looted.
Graffiti in three languages warning about the boss.
A vending-machine style dispenser that takes gold and gives out coin flips.
A room where the ceiling is the floor. Crawlers walk on it upside down.
HIDDEN_STAIR_SPOTS: behind a false wall at the back of a mob latrine
beneath a loose floor slab in a dead-end corridor
inside a sealed crawler safe room whose door only opens from the inside
at the bottom of a drowned shaft; requires a breath-hold or a spell
under the boss chamber, reached through a maintenance crawlspace
in plain sight, disguised as a decorative well
behind a wall of stacked corpses the janitors haven't reached yet
in the ceiling; the ladder drops only when weight leaves the room
inside a mimic pretending to be a stairwell. The real one is next to it
in a room that only appears on a Neighborhood Map
STORYLINES: A multi-level-marketing scheme run by the local bosses; every neighborhood has a 'consultant' recruiting.
A turf war between two mob types that spills across neighborhood borders. Crawlers are collateral.
A missing-crawler mystery; notes and personal effects turn up in a trail across the map.
A cult recruiting mobs and crawlers alike toward the city boss chamber.
A labor dispute among the mobs. The bosses are management.
A plague spreading through one mob type, visibly mutating them neighborhood by neighborhood.
A smuggling route for contraband running through the boroughs to a buyer at the center.
A reality-show subplot the System is running about a doomed mob romance.
